The Mauritian public will today decide the future leadership of their country. Over 1.3 million people are expected to vote and the turnout is expected to exceed the 78% in the 2014 election. The polls suggest a win for Pravind Jugnauth and MSM, however approval for the Alliance Parti Travailliste-PMSD has increased in the past week. The coalition between the deputy PM Xavier Luc Duval of PMSD and former PM Navin Ramgoolam of the Labour Party was formed a month ago to combat the vast popularity of the Jugnauth family. The influence that his father built up during his six terms in office has helped win his son support from large parts of the public. However, Jugnauth may have placed too much faith in the electorate by not forming an alliance with another party. It is usually required to form a coalition to be able to claim a majority vote. MSM were originally approached by the Labour Party to form an alliance but they were turned down. They subsequently joined with PMSD. This alliance between PMSD and the Labour Party has recently won more support as of late and seeks to bring a new age of economic development for Mauritius. If victorious Duval will take on the role of Prime Minister, while Ramgoolam, of the Labour Party, will be his deputy.
